title: Korea Institute of Energy Technology Act
full_text:
Chapter 1 General Provisions

Article 1 (Purpose)
The purpose of this Act is to establish the Korea Institute of Energy Technology to contribute to the advancement of national science and technology by training highly skilled professionals to lead innovation in the nation's energy science and technology and industrial ecosystem, and promoting educational and research exchanges at home and abroad and with industry.

Chapter 2 Establishment

Article 2 (Legal Entity)
The Korea Institute of Energy Technology (hereinafter referred to as "KENTECH") shall be a legal entity.

Article 3 (Establishment)
(1) KENTECH shall come into existence upon registration of its establishment at the location of its principal office.
(2) Matters necessary for the registration of the establishment of KENTECH and other registrations shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 4 (Articles of Incorporation)
(1) The articles of incorporation of KENTECH shall include the following matters:
1. Purpose.
2. Name.
3. Location of the principal office.
4. Matters concerning operations and their execution.
5. Matters concerning property and accounting.
6. Important matters concerning officers and employees.
7. Matters concerning the board of directors.
8. Matters concerning the university council.
9. Matters concerning amendments to the articles of incorporation.
10. Matters concerning the method of public notice.
11. Matters concerning dissolution and merger.
(2) KENTECH shall obtain authorization from the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment to amend its articles of incorporation. <Amended 2025.10.1>
(3) Before authorizing an amendment to the articles of incorporation under paragraph (2), the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment shall obtain the prior consent of the Minister of Education. <Amended 2025.10.1>

Article 5 (Support and Coordination, Etc.)
The Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment and the Korea Electric Power Corporation under the Korea Electric Power Corporation Act shall support and promote the development of KENTECH, and the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment shall coordinate and supervise the operations of KENTECH. <Amended 2025.10.1>

Chapter 3 Organization

Article 6 (Officers)
(1) KENTECH shall have no more than 15 directors, including one chairperson of the board and one President, and one auditor, and their terms of office shall be prescribed by the articles of incorporation.
(2) The directors and auditor shall be appointed by the board of directors as prescribed by the articles of incorporation, subject to approval by the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment. <Amended 2025.10.1>
(3) Before approving the appointment of directors or the auditor under paragraph (2), the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment shall obtain the prior consent of the Minister of Education. <Amended 2025.10.1>
(4) The chairperson of the board shall be appointed from among the directors as prescribed by the articles of incorporation.
(5) The chairperson of the board shall not concurrently serve as President of KENTECH.
(6) Officers other than the President or auditor shall not serve full time.
(7) The auditor shall audit the operations and accounts of KENTECH.

Article 7 (President)
(1) KENTECH shall have a President.
(2) The President shall represent KENTECH and oversee its operations.
(3) The President shall be appointed by the board of directors as prescribed by the articles of incorporation, subject to approval by the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment. <Amended 2025.10.1>
(4) Before approving the appointment of the President under paragraph (3), the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment shall obtain the prior consent of the Minister of Education. <Amended 2025.10.1>
(5) The duties and term of office of the President and other necessary matters shall be prescribed by the articles of incorporation.
(6) The President may concurrently serve as a faculty member or researcher.

Article 8 (Board of Directors)
(1) KENTECH shall have a board of directors to deliberate on and decide the following matters:
1. Matters concerning budgets and settlement of accounts.
2. Matters concerning the appointment and removal of officers.
3. Matters concerning the acquisition, disposition, and management of important property prescribed by the articles of incorporation.
4. Matters concerning amendments to the articles of incorporation.
5. Matters concerning the enactment, amendment, and repeal of important regulations.
6. Matters for which statutes, regulations, or the articles of incorporation require a resolution of the board of directors.
7. Other matters deemed necessary by the board of directors.
(2) The board of directors shall be composed of the chairperson of the board and the directors.
(3) The chairperson of the board shall convene meetings of the board of directors and preside over them.
(4) The auditor may attend meetings of the board of directors and state opinions.
(5) Other matters necessary for the board of directors shall be prescribed by the articles of incorporation.

Article 9 (University Council)
(1) KENTECH shall have a university council to deliberate on the following matters. However, its role concerning subparagraph 2 shall be limited to providing advice.
1. Matters concerning medium- and long-term development plans.
2. Important matters concerning the operation of curricula and research.
3. Important matters concerning the welfare of faculty members, staff members, and students.
4. Important matters concerning the operation of KENTECH prescribed by the articles of incorporation.
5. Other matters for which the President, the chairperson of the university council, or at least one-third of the incumbent council members request deliberation upon deeming them important to the operation of the school.
(2) The university council shall consist of at least 11 council members who can represent their respective constituencies, including faculty members, staff members (including researchers), and students, and may include alumni and persons who can contribute to the development of KENTECH. In such cases, the number of council members belonging to any one constituency shall not exceed one-half of the total prescribed membership of the council.
(3) Article 19-2(3) through (6) of the Higher Education Act shall apply mutatis mutandis to the chairperson and vice chairperson of the university council, the terms of office of council members, the submission of data, the preparation of minutes, etc. In such cases, "head of a school" shall be construed as "President."
(4) The university council shall communicate the results of its deliberations to the President, and the President shall refer matters requiring a resolution of the board of directors or matters deemed important to the board of directors.
(5) Other matters necessary for the organization and operation of the university council shall be prescribed by the articles of incorporation as prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Chapter 4 Finance and Accounting, Etc.

Article 10 (Fiscal Year)
The fiscal year of KENTECH shall correspond to the fiscal year of the State.

Article 11 (Contributions)
(1) The State, local governments, or public institutions under Article 4 of the Act on the Management of Public Institutions may provide contributions to KENTECH.
(2) Matters necessary for the payment and use of contributions under paragraph (1), etc. shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 12 (Transfer of State Property, Etc.)
(1) Notwithstanding the provisions of other Acts, the State may gratuitously transfer State property and goods for the establishment and operation of KENTECH, etc. However, State-owned cultural heritage and State-owned natural heritage under the proviso to Article 66 of the Act on the Preservation and Utilization of Cultural Heritage (including where it applies mutatis mutandis under Article 63 of the Act on the Preservation and Utilization of Natural Heritage) shall be excluded. <Amended 2023.8.8>
(2) Where necessary for the establishment and operation of KENTECH, etc., the State may, notwithstanding the provisions of other Acts, lend State property to KENTECH or permit KENTECH to use and derive income from it, without charge.
(3) Where the head of a central administrative agency intends to transfer State property pursuant to paragraph (1), the head shall consult with the Minister of Finance and Economy. <Amended 2025.10.1>
(4) Where property is lent or its use and the derivation of income from it are permitted without charge pursuant to paragraph (2), the details, conditions, procedures, etc. shall be determined in a contract between the agency administering the property and KENTECH.

Article 13 (Submission of Business Plans, Etc.)
(1) KENTECH shall, as prescribed by Presidential Decree, submit its business plan and budget to the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment for approval before the beginning of each business year. In such cases, business plans and budgets concerning academic affairs shall also be submitted to the Minister of Education. <Amended on October 1, 2025>
(2) KENTECH shall submit to the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment a statement of settlement of revenue and expenditure accounts for each business year examined by a certified public accountant or accounting firm designated by that Minister. In such cases, statements of settlement of revenue and expenditure accounts concerning academic affairs shall also be submitted to the Minister of Education. <Amended on October 1, 2025>
(3) Among the matters stated in a statement of settlement of accounts under paragraph (2), any of the following matters may be excluded from the accounting audit by a certified public accountant or accounting firm:
1. Research work constituting State secrets;
2. Work directly related to subparagraph 1;
3. Research work under projects commissioned by enterprises for which the entrusted enterprise or other relevant parties have requested confidentiality protection.

Article 14 (Shared Use of Research Facilities, Etc.)
KENTECH shall endeavor, in mutual consultation with other research institutions, universities, professional organizations, and other entities, to share the use of research facilities, equipment, and other resources in order to improve research productivity and efficiently utilize research facilities. In such cases, KENTECH may require the institution using such facilities, equipment, or resources to bear all or part of the costs.

Article 15 (Donations, Etc.)
(1) A person who donates land, research facilities, research equipment and materials, or other property to KENTECH may use that property jointly with KENTECH for a specified period.
(2) Matters necessary for procedures for donating land, research facilities, research equipment and materials, and other property, and for their shared use, shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 16 (Profit-Making Business, Etc.)
(1) KENTECH may conduct profit-making business as prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment, to the extent that such business does not interfere with its educational and research activities. <Amended on October 1, 2025>
(2) Profits from profit-making business under paragraph (1) shall be applied to the operation and research of KENTECH.

Article 17 (Establishment of a Fund, Etc.)
(1) Where necessary to raise and supply funds required for the efficient conduct of research and development in energy science and technology and the administration of academic affairs, KENTECH may establish a development fund (hereinafter referred to as the "Fund").
(2) The Fund shall be financed from the following sources:
1. Contributions or donations from persons other than the Government;
2. Returns from operation of the Fund;
3. Other income prescribed by Presidential Decree.
(3) The Fund shall be used for any of the following purposes:
1. Expenditure of funds for research and development in energy science and technology;
2. Establishment and operation of large educational and research facilities;
3. Expenditure of funds necessary for other projects prescribed by Presidential Decree to achieve the purposes for which the Fund was established.
(4) Other matters necessary for the operation and management of the Fund shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Chapter 5 Academic Affairs, Etc.

Article 18 (Faculty Members and Researchers)
(1) KENTECH shall have professors, associate professors, and assistant professors as faculty members, and may have visiting professors, lecturers, and other faculty members where necessary.
(2) KENTECH shall have researchers necessary to conduct research on energy science and technology.
(3) The qualifications of faculty members under paragraph (1) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 19 (Formulation of Appointment Plans for Gender Equality, Etc.)
(1) KENTECH shall formulate and implement policies necessary for gender equality in faculty appointments.
(2) To avoid an imbalance favoring a particular gender in faculty appointments, the President shall, every three years, formulate in consultation with the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment, and implement, plans necessary for affirmative action, including appointment plans specifying target appointment ratios by academic field. In such cases, the President shall submit the results of implementation to the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment each year. <Amended on October 1, 2025>
(3) Matters necessary for the formulation of plans under paragraph (2) and other relevant matters shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 20 (Appointment and Removal of Faculty Members)
(1) Faculty members of KENTECH shall be appointed and removed by the President as prescribed by the articles of incorporation.
(2) Faculty members of KENTECH may be appointed under contracts specifying terms such as the period of employment, salary, working conditions, and agreements on achievements and performance, as prescribed by the articles of incorporation.
(3) Where the appointment period of a faculty member is to expire, the President shall, no later than six months before its expiration, notify the faculty member that the appointment period will expire and that the faculty member may apply for a review for reappointment ("notify" means to give notice in writing; hereinafter the same shall apply in this Article).
(4) A faculty member who receives notice under paragraph (3) and wishes to be reappointed shall apply to the President for a review for reappointment within 15 days from the date of receipt of the notice.
(5) The President shall decide whether to reappoint the faculty member following a review for reappointment by the faculty personnel committee under Article 21(1) (hereinafter referred to as the "faculty personnel committee"), and shall notify the faculty member of that decision no later than two months before the expiration of the appointment period. In such cases, where the President decides not to reappoint the faculty member, the notice shall specifically state the intention not to reappoint and the grounds for refusing reappointment.
(6) When the faculty personnel committee reviews the reappointment of a faculty member under paragraph (5), it shall base its review on objective grounds prescribed by the academic regulations, such as assessments of the following matters. In such cases, the faculty member shall be given an opportunity during the review to appear before the faculty personnel committee and state opinions or to submit opinions in writing.
1. Matters concerning student education;
2. Matters concerning academic research;
3. Matters concerning industry-academia cooperation;
4. Matters concerning contributions and service.
(7) A faculty member whose reappointment has been refused and who wishes to contest the refusal may request a review by the Teachers' Appeals Review Committee under Article 7 of the Special Act on the Improvement of Teachers' Status and Protection of Educational Activities within 30 days from the date the faculty member becomes aware of the refusal.

Article 21 (Faculty Personnel Committee)
(1) A faculty personnel committee shall be established to deliberate on important personnel matters, including the appointment of faculty members of KENTECH.
(2) Matters necessary for the organization, functions, and operation of the faculty personnel committee shall be prescribed by the articles of incorporation.

Article 22 (Tenured Faculty Members)
(1) Following deliberation by the faculty personnel committee, the President may appoint faculty members who have received outstanding evaluations in education, research, industry-academia cooperation, and contributions and service, or faculty members recognized as authorities in a particular specialized field, as faculty members whose tenure is guaranteed until retirement age (hereinafter referred to as "tenured faculty members").
(2) Matters concerning the persons subject to review, evaluation periods, number of reviews, evaluation items, and evaluation methods for tenured faculty members shall be prescribed by the academic regulations.
(3) Article 20(3) through (7) shall apply mutatis mutandis to the procedures for reviewing tenured faculty members.

Article 23 (Students)
(1) The President shall, as prescribed by Presidential Decree, determine matters concerning KENTECH's student enrollment quotas, admission qualifications, admission procedures, and other relevant matters, obtain approval from the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment, and report those matters to the Minister of Education. <Amended on October 1, 2025>
(2) The President shall, as prescribed by Presidential Decree, formulate and implement measures to develop KENTECH students into creative energy specialists.

Article 24 (Degree Programs, Etc.)
(1) KENTECH shall offer doctoral, professional master's, master's, and bachelor's degree programs.
(2) For each program under paragraph (1), the President shall, as prescribed by Presidential Decree, determine matters concerning the length of study, semesters, number of instructional days, academic departments, majors, curricula, and other relevant matters, and report them to the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment and the Minister of Education. <Amended on October 1, 2025>
(3) Except as otherwise specifically provided for in this Act, the Higher Education Act shall govern the conferral of degrees, faculty qualifications, admission qualifications, admission procedures, and other relevant matters for the doctoral, professional master's, master's, and bachelor's degree programs under paragraph (1).
(4) The President shall, as prescribed by Presidential Decree, formulate and implement measures to promote KENTECH's international exchanges and cooperation and strengthen its international competitiveness in education and research.

Article 25 (Conferral of Degrees)
The President shall confer doctoral degrees, professional master's degrees, master's degrees, and bachelor's degrees as prescribed by the academic regulations.

CHAPTER 6 SUPPLEMENTARY PROVISIONS

Article 26 (Prohibition of Use of Similar Names)
No person other than KENTECH under this Act shall use the name Korea Institute of Energy Technology or any similar name.

Article 27 (Duty to Maintain Confidentiality)
No current or former officer or employee of KENTECH shall disclose or misappropriate any secret learned in the course of performing his or her duties.

Article 28 (Application Mutatis Mutandis of the Civil Act)
Except as provided in this Act, the provisions of the Civil Act concerning incorporated foundations shall apply mutatis mutandis to KENTECH.

Article 29 (Deeming Officers and Employees Public Officials for Purposes of Penalty Provisions)
Officers and employees of KENTECH shall be deemed public officials for purposes of applying Articles 129 through 132 of the Criminal Act.

CHAPTER 7 PENALTY PROVISIONS

Article 30 (Penalties)
A person who discloses or misappropriates a secret in violation of Article 27 shall be punished by imprisonment with or without labor for not more than three years or by a fine not exceeding 30 million won.

Article 31 (Administrative Fines)
(1) A person who uses the name Korea Institute of Energy Technology or any similar name in violation of Article 26 shall be subject to an administrative fine not exceeding five million won.
(2) The Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment shall impose and collect administrative fines under paragraph (1), as prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended on October 1, 2025>

ADDENDA <Act No. 17982, April 1, 2021>

Article 1 (Enforcement Date)
This Act shall enter into force one month after the date of its promulgation.

Article 2 (Transitional Measures)
(1) Where the educational foundation Korea Electric Power University of Technology, established under the Private School Act as at the time this Act enters into force, amends its articles of incorporation and obtains authorization from the Minister of Trade, Industry and Energy under Article 4 of this Act, it shall be deemed the Korea Institute of Energy Technology established under this Act.
(2) The educational foundation Korea Electric Power University of Technology that has obtained authorization from the Minister of Trade, Industry and Energy under paragraph (1) shall be deemed dissolved upon the establishment of the Korea Institute of Energy Technology, notwithstanding the provisions of the Private School Act concerning the dissolution and liquidation of corporations, and the Korea Institute of Energy Technology under this Act shall succeed to all property, rights, and obligations belonging to the educational foundation Korea Electric Power University of Technology. In such cases, the name of the educational foundation Korea Electric Power University of Technology appearing in registers and other public records concerning such property, rights, and obligations shall be deemed the name of the Korea Institute of Energy Technology under this Act.

Article 3 (Special Cases concerning Establishment)
Notwithstanding Article 4 of the Higher Education Act, the Korea Institute of Energy Technology may be established upon meeting the standards for facilities, equipment, faculty, and other matters as prescribed by Presidential Decree: Provided, That it shall meet the establishment standards under Article 4 of the Higher Education Act before the year in which its full complement of academic years is established.

ADDENDA (Act on the Preservation and Utilization of Cultural Heritage) <Act No. 19590, August 8, 2023>

Article 1 (Enforcement Date)
This Act shall enter into force on May 17, 2024.

Articles 2 through 8 Omitted.

Article 9 (Amendments to Other Acts)
(1) through (48) Omitted.
(49) The Korea Institute of Energy Technology Act is partially amended as follows:
The proviso to Article 12 (1) is amended to read as follows:
Provided, That State-owned cultural heritage and State-owned natural heritage under the proviso to Article 66 of the Act on the Preservation and Utilization of Cultural Heritage (including cases where that proviso applies mutatis mutandis pursuant to Article 63 of the Act on the Preservation and Utilization of Natural Heritage) shall be excluded.
(50) through (53) Omitted.

Article 10 Omitted.

ADDENDA (Government Organization Act) <Act No. 21065, October 1, 2025>

Article 1 (Enforcement Date)
This Act shall enter into force on the date of its promulgation: Provided, That, among the Acts amended pursuant to Article 7 of these Addenda, the portions amending Acts that were promulgated before this Act enters into force but have not yet entered into force shall enter into force on the respective enforcement dates of those Acts, and the following amended provisions shall enter into force on the dates specified in the respective subparagraphs:
1. The amended provisions in the following items shall enter into force on January 2, 2026: Provided, That, among the Acts amended pursuant to Article 7 of these Addenda (limited to portions relating to the amended provisions in items (a) and (b)), the portions amending Acts that were promulgated before the enforcement date specified in the main clause but have not yet entered into force as at that enforcement date shall enter into force on the respective enforcement dates of those Acts:
  (a) The amended provisions of Articles 19 (4), 23, 29 (1) 1, and 30;
  (b) The amended provisions of Articles 12 (2), 19 (3), 22, and the proviso to Article 29 (2) (limited to portions concerning the Minister of Finance and Economy and the Ministry of Finance and Economy);
  (c) The Acts amended pursuant to Article 7 of these Addenda (limited to portions relating to the amended provisions in items (a) and (b)).
2. Omitted.

Articles 2 through 6 Omitted.

Article 7 (Amendments to Other Acts)
(1) through (290) Omitted.
(291) The Korea Institute of Energy Technology Act is partially amended as follows:
In Article 4 (2) and (3), Article 5, Article 6 (2) and (3), Article 7 (3) and (4), the former part of Article 13 (1), the former part of paragraph (2) of that Article, the former and latter parts of Article 19 (2), Article 23 (1), Article 24 (2), and Article 31 (2), "Minister of Trade, Industry and Energy" is replaced with "Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment", respectively.
In Article 12 (3), "Minister of Economy and Finance" is replaced with "Minister of Finance and Economy".
In Article 16 (1), "Ordinance of the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy" is replaced with "Ordinance of the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment".
(292) through (626) Omitted.

Article 8 Omitted.
